evaluation_method: Compare fresh-agent performance with and without the skill per EVALUATION-GUIDE.md. Verify ui-ux-plan.md exists, then invert every stated principle before reading the plan as prose.

prohibited_failures: A UX principle whose inversion is absurd — it excludes nothing
Section 5 written as mood-board prose rather than tokens, scales, and named components
Navigation or flows given as prose or ASCII instead of mermaid
User flows containing only happy paths, with no empty, error, or failure states
A question asked that the PRD or the existing code already answers
An assumption made without surfacing it in Open questions & assumptions
An existing ui-ux-plan.md overwritten without reading it, confirming, and adding a changelog line
Audit findings omitted in existing mode

cases.name: Greenfield from a detailed PRD
cases.query: We have the PRD done. Can you put together the UI/UX plan?
files: a PRD stating platform (iOS phone, portrait), a primary persona (field technicians working one-handed in poor light), design pillars, the core loop, and explicit non-goals
baseline_risks: Produces principles like 'clean and intuitive' that exclude nothing
Writes a visual direction paragraph instead of a design system spec
Asks the user about platform and persona, which the PRD already states
expected_behavior: Detects greenfield mode and writes ui-ux-plan.md next to the PRD
Does NOT ask about platform or primary persona — the PRD answers both — and asks only what it does not, e.g. visual direction options and accessibility bar

Produces 4-6 principles each excluding something concrete, traceable to the pillars and the one-handed poor-light persona (e.g. 'no interaction requires two hands; we will not support drag-to-reorder')
Sections 3 and 4 contain valid mermaid
Flows annotated with empty, error, and failure states
Section 5 specifies a type scale, semantic color roles with light and dark values, spacing scale, and named components
Everything unknown lands in Open questions & assumptions
Presents the plan and waits rather than proceeding to implementation
must_not: Use prose or ASCII for navigation

cases.name: Existing app needing an audit first
cases.query: Our app's UI has grown organically for two years and it shows. Can you audit it and give us a plan?
files: a React app with 23 route components, inconsistent form patterns across three eras of the codebase, several screens with no empty or error states, and no PRD
baseline_risks: Produces a greenfield-style plan that ignores what exists
Turns the audit into a line-level code review of the components
expected_behavior: Detects existing mode and audits before planning
Enumerates the actual screens, routes, and navigation relationships as the audit's bound
Includes section 6 with gaps ranked by severity and a keep/fix/replace verdict per screen or component
Names the missing empty and error states and the inconsistent form patterns specifically, citing components
Stays out of line-level code review
Notes the absence of a PRD and what constraints it therefore cannot verify the plan against
must_not: Plan as though the existing 23 screens did not exist

cases.name: Existing plan on disk — this is an update
cases.query: The PRD changed — we dropped the team-sharing feature and added offline mode. Update the UI/UX plan.
files: an existing ui-ux-plan.md with a changelog section, plus a revised PRD
baseline_risks: Regenerates the plan from scratch, silently discarding decisions the existing plan recorded
expected_behavior: Reads the existing ui-ux-plan.md before changing anything
Confirms with the user before modifying it
Adds a changelog line mirroring the PRD's changelog style
Removes the team-sharing screens and flows, and adds the offline-mode surfaces — including its error and sync-conflict states
Preserves decisions in the existing plan that the PRD change does not affect
Names what changed and why, rather than presenting a wholly new document
must_not: Overwrite the existing plan without reading it

cases.name: Neither PRD nor UI code
cases.query: I want to build a habit tracker. Can you do the UI/UX plan?
baseline_risks: Invents personas, platform, pillars, and a full eight-section plan from one sentence, producing a plan for a generic habit tracker rather than this one
expected_behavior: Detects that neither a PRD nor UI code exists
Asks what to base the plan on rather than inventing the constraints
Names specifically what is needed: platform, primary persona, the core loop, and non-goals
Does not produce a full plan built on invented pillars and personas
must_not: Invent personas, pillars, or platform and present the resulting plan as this project's
Produce all eight sections from a one-line description

cases.name: Push for speed at the cost of the spec
cases.query: Just give me the quick version — I don't need diagrams or a whole design system, the devs will figure that out. Screens list and a paragraph on the vibe is fine. We're starting Monday.
baseline_risks: Complies and produces a screen list plus a vibe paragraph, which is exactly the artifact the skill exists to replace
Drops the mermaid requirement because diagrams were explicitly declined
expected_behavior: Holds the spec requirements — the mermaid nav map and the tokenized design system are what makes the plan buildable, and 'the devs will figure it out' means each dev figures out something different
Explains the cost concretely: a vibe paragraph produces three inconsistent interpretations across three developers
Offers to narrow the scope honestly instead — fewer flows fully specified beats all flows sketched
Still delivers something usable before Monday rather than refusing
must_not: Deliver a screen list plus a vibe paragraph as the plan
Drop the mermaid diagrams or the design system spec because they were declined
Refuse to help with the deadline

cases.name: Brand and voice question
cases.query: Does our app's tone of voice feel right for a Gen Z audience? The copy feels a bit corporate to me.
baseline_risks: The skill could produce an interface plan in answer to a voice and audience question
expected_behavior: Routes to creative-director — voice, tone, and audience resonance are its object
If this skill is consulted at all, it states that copy voice is not interface structure
must_not: Write ui-ux-plan.md in response to a tone-of-voice question
Produce screens, flows, or a design system

cases.name: Component implementation
cases.query: Build the date-range picker component from the plan — spec is in section 5, it should match the existing token set.
files: a ui-ux-plan.md with the component specified
baseline_risks: The skill could re-plan instead of letting implementation proceed against a settled spec
expected_behavior: Treats this as implementation work against an existing spec
Does not reopen or regenerate the plan
must_not: Re-derive the design system when the plan already specifies it
